simon: Ran an nsys trace on the perf regression repro (SERVE-562). TL;DR: a bunch of matmuls are unexpectedly falling back to small-workspace algos and overall token latency spikes. Sharing raw notes + logs below.

raj: can you paste the timeline and any cublaslt selection logs?

simon: pasted the trimmed timeline (nsys timeline view) + cublaslt stdout we capture. main anomalies: repeated workspace allocation failures and algorithm fallback events during attention matmul for seq_len ~1024.

simon: ```
# nsys extract (timeline slice)
[KERNEL] 0x7f.. cuBLASLtMatmul Algo=4 stream=0x3cuda Time=1.7ms
[KERNEL] 0x7f.. cuBLASLtMatmul Algo=1 stream=0x3cuda Time=3.9ms (fallback)
[MEM] cudaMallocAsync failed size=1048576 -> reported available_pool=0
[LOG] cublasLt: requested workspace=1MB, allocated=0 -> fallback to algo with no workspace
```

amy: that matches the repro I hit. The KV cache growth + our batching heuristic caused pad_to_max to jump to 1024 for a small fraction of requests, so matmul shapes went from 512->1024 and blew past our workspace budget.

sara: important: cublasLt often picks faster algos that need workspace. If workspace isn't provisioned we fallback to algo with higher time. The runtime currently uses a per-GPU transient pool sized to 16MB. For 1MB workspace per op and concurrency spikes, pool drains.

raj: do we have the algo-selection verbose logs? need algo IDs and workspace bytes per op.

simon: yes, here's the captured cublasLt selection lines from our environment var debug output:``` 
[cublasLt DEBUG] op=matmul lhs=(b=1,m=1024,k=4096) rhs=(b=1,k=4096,n=1024) candidate algo=4 workspaceNeeded=1048576 estTime=1.5ms
[cublasLt DEBUG] cudaMallocAsync returned nullptr for workspaceNeeded=1048576
[cublasLt DEBUG] fallback to algo=1 workspaceNeeded=0 estTime=3.9ms
```

amy: note the lhs/rhs dims — this is coming from KV cache + attention where k/v cache length doubled for a subset of requests (cached past tokens + new tokens). So peak shape is transient but still triggers expensive kernel selection.

raj: hypothesis: two vectors: (1) batching/padding policy that lets one long request force max pad for entire micro-batch, (2) insufficient workspace pool sizing / fragmentation. Both combine to cause a lot of small-workspace fallbacks.

sara: agree. Quick mitigation: 1) cap pad growth for micro-batches to 512 unless request explicitly asked for >512, 2) increase transient workspace pool to 64MB or implement slab allocator to reduce fragmentation, 3) emit cublasLt verbose only for candidate ops to avoid perf log spam.

simon: ran an experiment: increased pool to 64MB and re-ran single nsys trace. Median matmul latency dropped 30% on the hotspot and end-to-end token p95 dropped by ~18%. I'll attach numbers in doc later.

perf-bot: perf-summary: baseline p95=210ms -> after pool=64MB p95=172ms; p50 improved from 88ms->70ms. nsight timeline shows 40% fewer fallback kernels.

raj: nice. Longer term we should: - add a fallback policy that prefers small-workspace algos only when memory truly unavailable (not just transient allocation fail), - track per-op workspace demand histogram and expose in console.

amy: also check KV cache allocation strategy: we pre-allocate contiguous KV buffers per batch which causes occasional fragmentation when combined with workspace allocations. Maybe move to separate memory arenas for KV and workspace.

simon: action items: @raj can you run a follow-up nsys with CUBLASLT_ALGO_VERBOSE=1 + POOL_SIZE=64MB on the repro and post the trace? @amy can you instrument our batching heuristic to clamp pad_to_max to 512 for 2 weeks? I'll coordinate rollout to staging.

raj: on it. I'll post the nsys link when done. expected run in ~1h. :eyes:

amy: starting the batching clamp PR now. small test passed locally. :thumbsup:

sara: I'll draft the console metric for workspace demand histograms and a perf regression alert for sudden increases in fallback rate.

perf-bot: note: created ticket PERF-789 "cublaslt workspace histogram & fallback alert" and assigned to sara/raj/simon.

simon: thanks everyone. putting a short write-up + trace link in the ticket after raj uploads.

raj: uploaded trace: https://internal-nsys/traces/1759001111/simon-repro-1 (nsys report + profile).
